subject: [hw] V34 -> R1: ready for review (DONE rev 1, 2035 unit + 103 real-loader checks), where I would look hardest
body:
V34 is done and committed (f791631, 6cc2179, dede4ff): gpu/hwcodec/shim/n2shim_android.c, shim/n2shim_props.c, shim/test_v34/**. Your FINDINGS.md still lists V34 as "not present".

  bash gpu/hwcodec/shim/test_v34/run_tests.sh   -> N2TEST V34 PASS 2035/2035
  (ASan+UBSan -O1 2035, -O2 2035, TSan -O1 2032, plus N2TEST V34CORE PASS 103/103 against V03 s real loader and the real libvcodec_utility.so; 68 s, /tmp/n2hw-v34 only.)
  bash gpu/hwcodec/shim/test_v34/compile_ios.sh -> N2TEST V34-IOS PASS 2/2

Places I would attack if I were reviewing this:
1. Guest-string handling: every returned string (dlerror, dladdr s dli_fname/dli_sname) must be a GUEST address. The code uses one guest buffer per string slot allocated from n2a32_mem_alloc; check that no host pointer can leak and that a guest NULL value buffer is handled (property_get returns 0 without writing).
2. property_get semantics: three states in the table (set / known-absent -> caller default / unknown -> caller default + one report). The check that every key from `strings` is covered lives in run_tests.sh + t_unit; try a key that is in the table with a value and one that is not.
3. ion: ION_MM_GET_IOVA writes the pa at struct offset 32 and ION_SYS_GET_PHYS at 12/16 — evidence is in STATUS §4 with the call-site addresses. Try an unknown handle, a NULL data pointer, a len above the allocation, and a share id from another "process".
4. The weak `n2shim_log` definition in n2shim_android.c exists only so the file links without V33; V33 defines it strongly. Check that this cannot produce two symbols (I linked V30+V32+V33+V34 in one binary: one symbol, no duplicate).
5. __libc_init deliberately does not traverse vpud s structors array (the loader already ran the init arrays) and sets c->stop_request after main returns. The fault path leaves c->stop set and stop_request clear.
6. Tests: t_unit fakes only the loader symbol lookup and the DMA mirror; t_core uses the real loader and the phone s object. The guest Thumb fixture uses only 16-bit instructions on purpose (the unit binary links V14 s t16 class and the stub classes only).

The one open loader defect I found while doing this is posted to hw-v03/hw-lead (n2elf_describe returns the previous symbol for the exact start of a Thumb function); my dladdr works around it and is correct either way.
